exEn: I'm going to buy groceries after work.
note: The everyday word for buying food: handla mat. Handla om = to be about: Filmen handlar om en hund.

ex: Vi var på stan och {shoppade} hela dagen.
exEn: We were in town shopping all day.
note: sh is the sj-sound. Used for clothes and fun things; buying food is handla.

exEn: We're going to sell our old car.
note: Irregular: sålde, sålt.

exEn: I don't have any money left.
note: Always plural in Swedish: Pengarna räcker inte (The money isn't enough).

exEn: The ice cream costs twenty-five kronor.
note: Plural kronor, written kr or SEK: 25 kr. Krona also means crown.

ex: Priset är nitton kronor och nittio {öre}.
exEn: The price is nineteen kronor and ninety öre.
note: There are no öre coins any more, but prices still use them: 19,90 kr. Cash totals are rounded to whole kronor.

exEn: The machine only takes coins.
note: Same form in the plural: ett mynt, två mynt.

exEn: Can you break this bill?
note: The e drops in the plural: sedlar. In everyday speech: en hundralapp (a 100-kronor note).

exEn: Many stores don't take cash anymore.
note: Plural only. To pay cash = betala kontant.

exEn: Here you go, keep the change!
note: No plural in this sense. Also means gear (in a car).

exEn: I've left my card at home.
note: Same spelling as kort (short). Any card: vykort (postcard), körkort (driver's license).

ex: Hon fick ett {presentkort} på femhundra kronor.
exEn: She got a gift card worth five hundred kronor.

alt: can I pay with a card
can I pay with my card
ex: Jag har inga kontanter. {Kan jag betala med kort}?
exEn: I don't have any cash. Can I pay by card?
note: Cards are accepted almost everywhere in Sweden. Also: Tar ni kort?

exEn: You can send me the money by Swish.
note: Swish is the mobile payment app almost everyone in Sweden uses. Pronounced svisha.

exEn: Prices have gone up this year.
note: Also means prize: Hon vann första pris.

ex: Ursäkta, {hur mycket kostar det} att parkera här?
exEn: Excuse me, how much does it cost to park here?
note: Also: Vad kostar det? About a specific thing: Hur mycket kostar den?

exEn: That'll be a hundred and fifty kronor, please.
note: What the cashier says when telling you the total.

exEn: Students get a ten percent discount.
note: Stress on -batt. Also means a flower bed.

exEn: I bought the shoes on sale.
note: På rea = on sale. Det är rea! = There's a sale on! Short for realisation.

ex: Butiken har ett bra {erbjudande} på kaffe.
exEn: The store has a good deal on coffee.
note: From erbjuda (to offer). Stores advertise Veckans erbjudande (This week's offer).

exEn: You pay at the checkout over there.
note: Many supermarkets also have självscanning (self-scanning).

exEn: Would you like the receipt?
note: Keep it! You usually need it to return or exchange something.

ex: – {Var det bra så}? – Ja, det var allt.
exEn: – Will that be all? – Yes, that's everything.
note: Very common at shop and café counters. Literally: Was that good like that?

exEn: Do you need a bag?
note: Bags cost a few kronor at the checkout, so many people bring their own. A handbag is a väska.

ex: Ska vi ta en {kundvagn} eller en korg?
exEn: Shall we take a cart or a basket?
note: kund (customer) + vagn (cart); gn sounds like ngn. Some stores need a coin to unlock the carts.

exEn: I'm putting the fruit in the basket.
note: rg at the end sounds like rj. Online, your cart is varukorgen.

exEn: There's a long line at the checkout.
note: The k is hard here (from French queue). Many shops use a nummerlapp: take a number and wait.

en: to stand in line; to queue
exEn: We had to stand in line for half an hour.
note: Hard k, as in kö (unlike köpa, which starts with the tj-sound).

ex: Vad har ni för {öppettider} i jul?
exEn: What are your opening hours over Christmas?
note: Almost always plural; the singular öppettid is rare.

ex: Affären {har öppet} till nio i kväll.
exEn: The store is open until nine tonight.
note: The opposite is ha stängt. Signs on doors just say Öppet / Stängt.

exEn: The store sells goods from all over the world.
note: Mostly plural: varor = goods. Not the same word as the verb vara (to be).

exEn: What size are you?
note: Sizes are European: Jag har storlek 40 i skor (I take a size 40 shoe).

sv: Finns den i en större storlek?
en: do you have it in a bigger size?
alt: do you have it in a bigger size
do you have it in a larger size
does it come in a bigger size
do you have a bigger size
ipa: fɪnːs dɛn ɪ ɛn ˈstœrːɛ ˈstuːˌɭeːk
ex: Tröjan är för liten. {Finns den i en större storlek}?
exEn: The sweater is too small. Do you have it in a bigger size?
note: Smaller: i en mindre storlek. Literally: Does it exist in a bigger size?

exEn: Can I try on these pants?
note: Also to try in general: Prova den här kakan! (Try this cake!)

exEn: Excuse me, where are the fitting rooms?
note: prova (to try on) + hytt (cabin).

ex: – Kan jag hjälpa dig? – Nej tack, {jag tittar bara}.
exEn: – Can I help you? – No thanks, I'm just looking.
note: The polite answer when a shop assistant offers help.

ex: Kan jag {byta} tröjan mot en mindre?
exEn: Can I exchange the sweater for a smaller one?
note: byta mot = exchange for. Also byta tåg (change trains). Past: bytte, bytt.

ex: Jag vill {lämna tillbaka} de här skorna.
exEn: I'd like to return these shoes.
note: Stress on tillbaka. Få pengarna tillbaka = to get a refund.

ex: Telefonen gick sönder, så jag {reklamerade} den.
exEn: The phone broke, so I took it back as faulty.
note: False friend: not reclaim. You can complain to the seller about faulty goods for up to three years.

exEn: The phone has a two-year warranty.
note: Stress on -ti. Definite form: garantin.

ex: Jag köpte en {begagnad} cykel på nätet.
exEn: I bought a used bike online.
note: gn sounds like ngn: be-GANG-nad.

ex: I helgen ska vi gå på {loppis}.
exEn: This weekend we're going to a flea market.
note: Short for loppmarknad. Gå på loppis = go to a flea market or second-hand sale.

ex: Jag måste köpa en {present} till Anna.
exEn: I have to buy a present for Anna.
note: Stress on -sent. A Christmas present is a julklapp.

exEn: I'm saving money for a trip.
note: Also to save a file, and to keep: Spara kvittot! (Keep the receipt!)

ex: Hon {tjänar} bra på sitt nya jobb.
exEn: She makes good money at her new job.
note: Starts with the tj-sound. Also means to serve.

ex: Vi {har råd} med en större lägenhet nu.
exEn: We can afford a bigger apartment now.
note: ha råd med + noun, ha råd att + verb. Jag har inte råd = I can't afford it.

ex: Kan jag {låna} hundra kronor av dig?
exEn: Can I borrow a hundred kronor from you?
note: låna av = borrow from. To lend is låna ut: Kan du låna ut din cykel?

ex: Vi tog ett {lån} för att köpa huset.
exEn: We took out a loan to buy the house.
note: ta ett lån = take out a loan. A mortgage is ett bolån.

exEn: I need to open a bank account.
note: Often just kontot: Pengarna finns på kontot.
